pageCache.pageTitle: Welcome to WGPS - Woodford Green Preparatory School
pageCache.text:
Welcome to WGPS
Welcome to Woodford Green Preparatory; our happy, vibrant and thriving school.
At WGPS, we believe every child is capable of achieving great things. We encourage our pupils to strive for their very best through a commitment to academic rigour and excellence, without compromising on the broad range of opportunities and experiences within the curriculum and co-curriculum, which create an innovative and progressive learning environment.
Pupils learn best when they are happy and feel secure. Our talented and dedicated staff work hard to ensure that each pupil is supported through personalised pastoral care and personal development.
Our broad and exciting curriculum is designed to stimulate a lifelong love of learning. Pupils not only become knowledgeable and intellectually curious but also develop independence, resilience, open-mindedness, and kindness. This is reflected in our most recent ISI Inspection Report, which states, "The social development and collaboration of pupils is excellent. There is a profound culture of care and kindness across the whole community, and relationships are warm and mutually supportive."
It is a pleasure and privilege to welcome you to our school. Please do contact us to find out more about our excellent school.
Our School

Our Motto, Mission and Values
Our Motto
"Let Each Flame Burn Brighter"
Our Mission
WGPS is a school where there is a culture of kindness, inclusivity, high ambition, and a breadth of opportunity that cultivates a skill set in our pupils that firmly prepares them to be active citizens and lifelong learners in our rapidly changing world.
Our Values
Our school values, developed in collaboration with pupils, parents, staff, and governors, define who we are and what we stand for. Written in a way that is accessible to all pupils, they are at the heart of everything we do.
Guided by our core values, we strive to:
We are kind
We use good manners
We are honest
We explore our ideas
We can work independently
We are always learning
We use our initiative
We welcome new challenges
We use our imagination
We always try our best
We celebrate each others’ successes
Our School

pageCache.pageTitle: Building a Rights Respecting Community at Woodford Green Prep - News Blog - Woodford Green Preparatory School
pageCache.text:
News Blog
Building a Rights Respecting Community at Woodford Green Prep
The UNICEF UK Rights Respecting Schools Award (RRSA) is based on the principles of equality, dignity, respect, non-discrimination and participation. A Rights Respecting School is a community where children’s rights are learned, taught, practised, respected, protected and promoted.
At Woodford Green Prep, we are committed to nurturing our learners to improve well-being and to develop every child’s talents and abilities to their full potential. At WGPS we already offer so much that reinforces the rights respecting message: we use Zones of Regulation; we have a variety of platforms to obtain pupil voice which we can then use to inform decision-making; we have robust Safeguarding systems and protocols in place.
The RRSA Award provides a clear framework which corroborates what we are already doing in school, and it provides fantastic additional opportunities for collaboration which will further strengthen the bonds within our whole-school community.
I am delighted to share that our school is embarking on its journey towards achieving the UNICEF UK Rights Respecting Schools Award. This will entail a whole-school community commitment to learning about rights and modelling rights and respect in all its relationships, whether between adults and pupils, between pupils, or between adults.
Our first step is to achieve Bronze accreditation, with a view to achieving Silver and eventually Gold. We are very excited about promoting the child rights-based approach which we fully believe will support our pupils to be reflective, empathetic and resilient global citizens.
We believe this work is important because it gives children a shared language for understanding fairness, responsibility and respect, helping them to navigate relationships, challenges and decision-making with confidence both in school and beyond.

pageCache.pageTitle: Netball News - News Blog - Woodford Green Preparatory School
pageCache.text:
News Blog
Netball News
The WGPS Netball League has got off to a fantastic start this term, with 30 children from Years 5 and 6, both boys and girls, taking part. So far, we have hosted Churchfields, Avon House, and St Antony’s, and it has been wonderful to see everyone enjoying the friendly competition within our local community.
The uptake in our morning netball club has also been phenomenal, this week alone, over 50 children attended, including more boys than ever before who are keen to get involved in the sport.
We are equally proud of our younger players. Several of our Year 3 pupils have joined the Essex Open Development Squad, while a number of pupils in Years 5 and 6 have been selected for the Essex Open Performance Squad and are already taking part in competitive matches on Saturday mornings.
One of our pupils has also been selected to play for London Pulse and now trains at the Chigwell School Hub, an incredible achievement!
Congratulations also go to our Netball League Players of the Match for their fantastic performances and teamwork on court.
It is brilliant to see so many of our pupils embracing netball, developing their skills, and achieving great success both in and outside of school.

pageCache.pageTitle: Carol Service - News Blog - Woodford Green Preparatory School
pageCache.text:
News Blog
Carol Service
Our annual Carol service has brought our Christmas festivities to a close again this year. What a treat to see all of Y3-6 at All Saints Church, Woodford Wells celebrating Christmas and delivering a moving performance based loosely on King’s College, Cambridge, Nine Lessons and Carols. Our Head Boy and Girl and Deputies, and Y5 read beautifully. Both Choirs performed their own angelic rendition of songs based around the Virgin Mary and the meaning of Christmas. Y3&4 sang a jazzy version of Away in a Manger and Y5&6 sang the most beautifully plaintive song written originally in the 1600s for the Huron people of Canada. The boys began the song and the girls echoed the melody singing in canon (many overlapping layers of sound) which created a tempered, calm and soothing effect perfect for reflection at Christmas time. To round off the service, after singing three traditional carols, the whole school celebrated the birth of Christ through their song Ring Out the Bells. Again the boys and girls echoed individual singing lines singing in canon together. The effect was magical to hear a chorus of 180 children all singing, not only together but also in harmony with each other.
May the harmony continue into our New Year both within the school and outside. Merry Christmas from the Music Department and thank you for your continued support.
We look forward to further engagements starting with our internal Whole School Singing competition two weeks into January followed by a Teatime concert on Tuesday 3rd February, our participation in the Stratford Festival of Music on Monday 8th February and our joint venture with Chigwell School at the prestigious London venue Cadogan Hall Tuesday 10th February.

pageCache.text:
Music
Music is good for your health!
It is becoming better known that music helps a child’s development in many ways. Music helps children to make connections between creative and analytical thinking; it helps develop the ability to process and retain information and improves a child’s hand-ear-eye co-ordination. Music can encourage a feeling of empathy and emotional awareness as well as improve a child’s ability to concentrate.
We aim for all of our pupils to develop a love of music, an appreciation of it and a sense of community within the department and school. We nurture children to develop musical language and knowledge and key skills that will aid their all-round educational learning. Neurological research suggests that pupils who are actively involved in music also manage to achieve a higher academic level.
Performing is a key part of being a musician and we aim to provide a vibrant, supportive music department through the curriculum and through our numerous and varied extra-curricular ensembles. There are opportunities to take part in Choirs, Orchestra, Jazz Band, Brass group, String ensemble, Guitar ensemble, Saxophone group or just playing solos in assembly. All musicians are welcome to participate in our ensembles even if they learn outside school. Many children develop ad hoc groups by taking initiative and organising themselves. We have concerts both formal and informal, carol services, competitions and festivals, all of which are supported by a team of peripatetic music teachers offering tuition on a wide spectrum of orchestral instruments, piano and voice.
Music is a creative, yet logical, subject. All children are warmly invited to come and learn in our department and to develop, through music a love of life, a feeling of acceptance, and a sense of fun!
Further information on the Music Department and individual vocal and instrumental lessons can be found in the 'Parent' section of this website, which is accessed at the top right of the screen.

pageCache.text:
Science
We have hands-on, investigative experiences, through a child-led approach. This allows our pupils to retain and develop their natural sense of curiosity about the world around them.
Our Science curriculum allows us to develop a set of attitudes, which will promote scientific ways of thinking, including open-mindedness, perseverance, objectivity and a recognition of the importance of teamwork. We aim to begin to build up a body of scientific knowledge and understanding, which will serve as a foundation for future enquiry. We encourage our pupils to make meticulous observation, make and test hypotheses and design fair and controlled experiments, from which they can draw meaningful conclusions.
We facilitate a STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering and Maths) Week during the Summer term with the whole school taking part.

pageCache.text:
Curriculum
Our curriculum aims to help develop the children to become lifelong learners, who can work independently and solve problems. We encourage a ‘growth mindset’ where pupils learn the skills of hard work, taking risks, being resilient, learning from failure, as well as making sure that they do the very best they can. The process of learning is equally important as to what they learn, as well as being broad and balanced.
Our curriculum sits hand in hand with tracking each pupil’s academic progress and is designed to set them up for moving into selective senior school entry. Working from the endpoint and then back through the year groups, each year of learning is carefully built upon the last. The end result is that our pupils receive a very high number of offers from selective senior schools and are very well prepared for enjoying their future studies.
We study all the National Curriculum subjects. French is taught from Year 2 onwards, with Spanish for our Year 6 pupils. Pupils are taught many of the subjects by their form teacher which allows for cross-curricular linkage, with additional subject specialist teachers for music, art, languages and sport. As a truly independent school we are able to choose the very best aspects of the National Curriculum and design learning opportunities to reflect carefully balanced and in-depth WGPS approach. This, in turn, provides support and challenge for all our pupils.
There are also a large number of extra-curricular opportunities which allow additional pathways for pupils to explore a width of experiences.
As a result, our boys and girls enter secondary school not only equipped with a wide range of experiences but a positive attitude to learning that will take them long into later life.

Teatime Club Registration
WOODFORD GREEN PREPARATORY SCHOOL TEATIME CLUB REGISTRATION
Terms and Conditions relating to Woodford Green Preparatory School Afterschool Provision (also referred to as Teatime Club).
Parents/carers who complete the online registration form are agreeing to these terms and conditions. Registration forms must be completed in full before your child can be allocated a place. This includes accepting these terms and conditions.
The Club’s policies and procedures reflect the school policies and procedures and parents can read the extended School’s policies and procedures on the School Website.
Teatime Club aims to provide a stimulating and creative atmosphere for your children with the emphasis being on play. We provide safe, high-quality childcare with regard to levels of staffing and health and safety of premises. This Club provides a quality care service where every child is respected as an individual. We feel strongly that the needs of the child should be the primary focus of the Club.
Sibling Club (EYFS and Years 1 & 2) is run between 3pm – 3.30pm. Sibling Club is only available for children with older siblings in Years 3 – 6. Children who are only attending the Sibling Club are to be picked up at 3.30pm promptly from the Foundation One entrance (East Door).
Any child not collected at 3.30pm will have to attend Teatime Club (if there is availability; if not, your child will be supervised by a member of the Senior Leadership Team and for this service we will charge £6.00 per 15 minutes).
If an adult is collecting who is not a ‘named adult’ we do ask that you inform the school so that your child can be released.
Teatime Club is open for any child at WGPS in Years 1 to 6 (a separate EYFS teatime club is also available) and takes place in the Hall. Occasionally due to concerts or other events, the Teatime Club will be moved to a Classroom. Parents/carers must use the Foundation One entrance (East Door) for collection and ring the bell when they arrive at the door.
Teatime Club starts at 3.30pm when the children are taken to the Hall by a member of staff. Teatime Club is divided into three sessions: the first two sessions run from 3.30pm – 4.30pm and 4.30pm -5.30pm. The cost of each of these sessions is £6.00. A third session from 5.30pm to 6.00pm runs on Mondays to Thursdays only and the cost for this session is £3.00.
A late collection charge is applied when a parent picks up their child late (after 6pm or after 5.30 on Fridays). This is £15.00 per fifteen minutes or part thereof. Please ensure that you have emergency systems in place in case of unforeseen circumstances and that you contact Teatime Club if there has been any emergency. Please either telephone the School Reception which is manned until 5pm every night, or after 5pm please call 0208 506 5196 (please note, this number is only to be used after 5pm).
Places are allocated in the order that Registration Forms are received. Parents who make late or ad-hoc bookings will only be notified if their child cannot be accommodated .
There will always be a WGPS staff member present who has undertaken appropriate First Aid Training. There is a very well stocked first aid box available to all staff. In addition, all staff have received appropriate training on how to deal with and record accidents and emergencies. If your child has had an accident whilst at Sibling/Teatime Club, it will be recorded on our green forms and passed on to the School Nurse the next day. You will be informed that evening of any accidents.
Parents/carers must ensure that all details on the registration form are accurate and up-to-date. Any changes must be made in writing to teatime@wgprep.co.uk
We would also ask that you keep Teatime Club records up-to-date by noting any changes to medicines, allergies or medical conditions that are stated on your child’s Registration Form.
Staff encourage positive behaviour through praise and appreciation of children’s achievements. The principles outlined in the Woodford Green Preparatory School Behaviour Policy are adhered to in both Sibling and Teatime clubs.
Appropriate sanctions will be applied where children do not adhere to instructions from the staff. For example, they will be given time out from activities and then parents informed (verbally and written where appropriate).
We aim to deal with all complaints by mutual agreement within the Club; please discuss any concerns first with the staff on duty. Should you feel that your complaint has not been adequately dealt with, or is of a particularly serious or sensitive nature, you should follow the Complaints Procedure as outlined on our School Website.
Tea (sandwiches, fruit, biscuit/cake with squash/water) will be served between 3.30- 4.30pm.
The Teatime Club will not run on days or half days when the School is closed to pupils. If your child is unable to attend a pre-booked session, you must notify the School via teatime@wgprep.co.uk
If your child is absent from school you must, when phoning the school, mention that they will also be absent from Teatime Club.
At the time of booking you will be prompted to select specific days/dates which you would like your child to attend. If your child is unable to attend for any reason you will not be entitled to a refund.
All Teatime Club sessions (including pre-booked, late bookings and sessions booked due to unforeseen circumstances) will be added to your termly invoice.
